questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: To design a single-layer quarter-wave anti-reflection coating on glass ($n_g = 1.69$) in air ($n_a = 1.00$) for normal incidence, the ideal refractive index $n_c$ of the coating material is
questions.explanationEn: For equal reflected amplitudes from the air-coating and coating-glass interfaces to cancel completely at quarter-wave thickness, we require $n_c = \sqrt{n_a n_g} = \sqrt{1.00 \times 1.69} = 1.30$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Two identical massless springs of force constant $k$ are connected to a block of mass $m$ first in parallel and then in series. The ratio of the angular frequency in the parallel arrangement to that in the series arrangement is
questions.explanationEn: In parallel, $k_p = 2k$; in series, $k_s = k/2$. Hence $\frac{\omega_p}{\omega_s} = \sqrt{\frac{k_p}{k_s}} = \sqrt{\frac{2k}{k/2}} = \sqrt{4} = 2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a high-$Q$ damped harmonic oscillator ($Q \gg 1$), the fractional energy lost per complete oscillation cycle, $\frac{|\Delta E|}{E}$, is approximately
questions.explanationEn: By definition, $Q = 2\pi \frac{\text{Energy stored}}{\text{Energy dissipated per cycle}} = \frac{2\pi E}{|\Delta E|}$, so $\frac{|\Delta E|}{E} = \frac{2\pi}{Q}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: When unpolarized light is incident on a planar air-glass interface at Brewster's angle, the reflected light is completely linearly polarized with its electric field vector
optionsEn: parallel to the plane of incidence
at $45^\circ$ to the plane of incidence
perpendicular to the plane of incidence
questions.explanationEn: At Brewster's angle, the $p$-polarized component (parallel to the plane of incidence) has zero reflectance ($R_p = 0$), so the reflected beam contains only the $s$-polarized component, whose electric field is perpendicular to the plane of incidence.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident normally on a single slit of width $a \gg \lambda$. The angular width of the central diffraction maximum (between the two first-order minima) is approximately
questions.explanationEn: The first-order minima occur at $\sin\theta = \pm \frac{\lambda}{a} \approx \pm \frac{\lambda}{a}$. The full angular width between them is $\Delta\theta = 2\theta_1 \approx \frac{2\lambda}{a}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A uniform solid cylinder of mass $m$ and radius $r$ rolls without slipping near the bottom of a fixed concave cylindrical surface of radius $R$ ($R > r$). The angular frequency of small oscillations is
questions.explanationEn: Let $\theta$ be the angular displacement of the cylinder's center from the vertical. Its center moves on an arc of radius $(R - r)$ with speed $v = (R - r)\dot{\theta}$, and rolling without slipping gives $\omega_{\text{spin}} = v/r$. Total kinetic energy is $T = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}mr^2\right)\frac{v^2}{r^2} = \frac{3}{4}m(R-r)^2\dot{\theta}^2$, and potential energy is $U \approx \frac{1}{2}mg(R-r)\theta^2$. Conservation of energy yields $\ddot{\theta} + \frac{2g}{3(R-r)}\theta = 0$, so $\omega = \sqrt{\frac{2g}{3(R-r)}}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A light source emits two closely spaced wavelengths $\lambda_1 = 600.0\text{ nm}$ and $\lambda_2 = 600.6\text{ nm}$ of equal intensity and illuminates a Michelson interferometer. The distance through which the movable mirror must be displaced between two consecutive positions of zero fringe visibility is
questions.explanationEn: Between consecutive minima of fringe visibility, the mirror displacement $\Delta d$ satisfies $2\Delta d \left(\frac{1}{\lambda_1} - \frac{1}{\lambda_2}\right) = 1 \implies \Delta d \approx \frac{\bar{\lambda}^2}{2\Delta\lambda} = \frac{(600 \times 10^{-9})^2}{2(0.6 \times 10^{-9})} = 3.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m} = 0.30\text{ mm}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A particle moves in the $xy$-plane according to $x(t) = a\cos(\omega t)$ and $y(t) = a\cos\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)$. The Cartesian equation of the elliptical trajectory traced by the particle is
questions.explanationEn: Using the standard Lissajous elimination $\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{a^2} - \frac{2xy}{a^2}\cos\delta = \sin^2\delta$ with $\delta = \frac{\pi}{3}$ ($\cos\delta = \frac{1}{2}$, $\sin^2\delta = \frac{3}{4}$) directly yields $x^2 + y^2 - xy = \frac{3}{4}a^2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A Fresnel zone plate has its primary (brightest) focal length $f_1 = 45\text{ cm}$ for monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$. The next strongest focal length $f_3$ of this zone plate for the same wavelength is
questions.explanationEn: A zone plate has multiple foci at $f_k = \frac{r_1^2}{(2k - 1)\lambda} = \frac{f_1}{2k - 1}$ for $k = 1, 2, 3, \dots$ Thus the next focus after $f_1$ is $f_3 = \frac{f_1}{3} = \frac{45}{3} = 15\text{ cm}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A plane transmission diffraction grating with grating element $d$ is illuminated normally by polychromatic light. The angular dispersion $\frac{d\theta}{d\lambda}$ in the $m$-th order spectrum at diffraction angle $\theta$ is
questions.explanationEn: Differentiating the grating equation $d\sin\theta = m\lambda$ with respect to $\lambda$ gives $d\cos\theta\,\frac{d\theta}{d\lambda} = m \implies \frac{d\theta}{d\lambda} = \frac{m}{d\cos\theta}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A taut string of length $L$ fixed at $x = 0$ and $x = L$ vibrates in its third harmonic with displacement $y(x, t) = A\sin\left(\frac{3\pi x}{L}\right)\cos(\omega t)$. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: Points at $x = L/6$ and $x = L/2$ oscillate with a phase difference of $\pi$
All points between $x = 0$ and $x = L/3$ oscillate in phase with each other
Including both fixed endpoints, there are $4$ nodes along the string
The net average energy flux across $x = L/3$ is non-zero
questions.explanationEn: Nodes occur at $3\pi x / L = n\pi \implies x = 0, L/3, 2L/3, L$ ($4$ nodes, True). Within any single loop $(0, L/3)$, $\sin(3\pi x/L) > 0$, so all points move in phase (True). At $x = L/6$, $\sin(\pi/2) = +1$; at $x = L/2$, $\sin(3\pi/2) = -1$, giving a $\pi$ phase difference (True). A pure standing wave carries zero net energy flux across any point (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a thin converging lens of focal length $f > 0$ placed in air, which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: A diverging beam incident on the lens can never form a real image
A real object placed at distance $u < f$ produces a virtual, erect, and magnified image
The minimum distance between a real object and its real image is $4f$
A real object placed at distance $u = 2f$ produces a real, inverted image of unit magnification ($m = -1$)
questions.explanationEn: For $u = -2f$, $v = +2f$ and $m = v/u = -1$ (True). Minimum real object-to-image distance is $4f$ (True). For $|u| < f$, $v < 0$ and $m = f/(f - |u|) > +1$, giving a virtual, erect, magnified image (True). Any real object at $|u| > f$ emits a diverging beam that the lens focuses to a real image (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In a Michelson interferometer using an extended monochromatic source of wavelength $\lambda$, the two mirrors $M_1$ and $M_2$ are adjusted to be strictly perpendicular (producing concentric circular Haidinger fringes). Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: When $d$ is decreased toward zero, the circular fringes shrink and disappear into the center
The angular radius of a circular fringe increases as the path difference $2d$ increases
The optical path difference for rays inclined at angle $\theta$ to the axis is $2d\cos\theta$, where $d$ is the separation between $M_1$ and the virtual image $M_2'$
A compensating glass plate of the same thickness and refractive index as the beam splitter is used so both beams traverse equal optical paths in glass (essential for white-light fringes)
questions.explanationEn: The compensating plate equalizes glass dispersion in both arms for white light (True). The inclined-ray path difference is $2d\cos\theta$ (True). Since $2d\cos\theta = m\lambda$, at the center ($\theta = 0$) the order is $m_0 = 2d/\lambda$; decreasing $d$ lowers $m_0$, causing fringes to collapse into the center (True), whereas increasing $d$ makes fringes emerge and expand outward, while the angular radius of the *first* ring around center actually *decreases* as $\theta_1 \approx \sqrt{\lambda/d}$ (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding the polarization of electromagnetic waves and birefringent waveplates is/are correct?
optionsEn: Unpolarized light can be distinguished from circularly polarized light using only a single linear polarizer
Only transverse waves can be polarized; longitudinal sound waves in air cannot be polarized
When circularly polarized light passes through a rotating ideal linear polarizer, the transmitted intensity remains constant
A quarter-wave plate converts circularly polarized light into linearly polarized light regardless of the orientation of its optic axis
questions.explanationEn: Polarization is exclusive to transverse waves (True). Circularly polarized light transmits $I_0/2$ through a linear polarizer at any angle (True), which is identical to unpolarized light, so a single linear polarizer cannot distinguish them (False—a quarter-wave plate + analyzer is needed). A quarter-wave plate removes the $\pm\pi/2$ phase difference of circularly polarized light, converting it to linear polarization (True).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In a Newton's rings experiment with air film using light of wavelength $600\text{ nm}$ and a plano-convex lens of radius of curvature $R = 1.0\text{ m}$, the difference $D_{10}^2 - D_4^2$ between the squares of the diameters of the $10^{\text{th}}$ and $4^{\text{th}}$ dark rings is ______ $\text{mm}^2$. (Round off to 1 decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: Using $D_{m+p}^2 - D_m^2 = 4p\lambda R$ with $p = 10 - 4 = 6$, $\lambda = 600 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}$, and $R = 1.0\text{ m}$ gives $4 \times 6 \times 6 \times 10^{-7} = 1.44 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}^2 = 14.4\text{ mm}^2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Linearly polarized light passes through an ideal analyzer, and the transmitted intensity is $75\%$ of the incident intensity. The acute angle between the incident polarization direction and the transmission axis of the analyzer is ______ degrees. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By Malus's law, $\cos^2\theta = 0.75 = \frac{3}{4} \implies \cos\theta = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \implies \theta = 30^\circ$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Two sound waves have intensity levels of $76\text{ dB}$ and $60\text{ dB}$. The ratio of the intensity of the louder sound to that of the quieter sound is ______. (Round off to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: Since $\beta_2 - \beta_1 = 10\log_{10}(I_2/I_1) = 16\text{ dB}$, we obtain $\frac{I_2}{I_1} = 10^{1.6} \approx 39.81$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A wave in a one-dimensional medium obeys the dispersion relation $\omega(k) = \sqrt{4k^2 + 9}$ (in SI units). The phase velocity of the wave at wavenumber $k = 2\text{ m}^{-1}$ is ______ $\text{m/s}$. (Round off to 1 decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: At $k = 2\text{ m}^{-1}$, $\omega = \sqrt{4(4) + 9} = 5\text{ rad/s}$. Thus $v_p = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{5}{2} = 2.5\text{ m/s}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A transverse traveling wave on a string is described by $y(x, t) = 0.02\sin(4x - 60t)$, where $x$ and $y$ are in meters and $t$ is in seconds. The speed of the wave is ______ $\text{m/s}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Comparing with $A\sin(kx - \omega t)$ gives $k = 4\text{ m}^{-1}$ and $\omega = 60\text{ rad/s}$. Thus $v = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{60}{4} = 15\text{ m/s}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Two identical sonometer wires are initially tuned in unison to a fundamental frequency of $400\text{ Hz}$. If the tension in one of the wires is increased by $2\%$ while keeping all other parameters unchanged, the beat frequency produced when both wires are plucked simultaneously is ______ $\text{Hz}$. (Round off to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: Since $f \propto \sqrt{T}$, the new frequency of the tightened wire is $f' = 400\sqrt{1.02} \approx 403.98\text{ Hz}$. The beat frequency is $f' - f = 403.98 - 400 = 3.98\text{ Hz}$.
